_comment: Cross-port parity classification for the 20 frozen goldens (7 biosphere + 13 station). Authored in Phase-7 Step 0 (P7.0) by inspecting each scenario's reachable evaluation graph (flows + resolver + schedule + scenario data) for transcendental ops. The `float_tier` is the tier for FLOAT TRAJECTORIES; the Tier-0 structural gate (see `_tier0`) is EXACT for every scenario regardless. Rule (advisor): classify by the ops the simulator EXECUTES, not the closed-form solution — a geometric contraction d_n=d0*(1-k*dt)^n is n sequential multiplies (IEEE basic ops, bit-identical across ports), NOT a pow() call, so it is Tier 1. Only a `math.{sin,cos,exp,log,pow,sqrt,tan}` / `**` in the per-step graph drops a scenario to Tier 2. `band`/`floor` are null until MEASURED (Tier-2 tolerances are measured, never derived). Step-3 (P7.3) measured the three standalone-sibling Tier-2 bands (power / power_self_discharge / thermal) via the propagated ±1-ULP transcendental SENSITIVITY (`measure_tier2_bands.py`), NOT the direct Rust-vs-Python deviation — which reads 0.0 on one machine because both call the same system libm (a same-libm artifact, not a cross-libm measurement). The band sits above that sensitivity; `test_crossport.py` re-measures and asserts band > sensitivity. Step-6 (P7.6) wired the whole parity suite into CI: the dedicated `crossport` job (Ubuntu, both toolchains) runs every `skipif cargo` comparison, so the bands are now enforced against glibc-Rust vs the UCRT-generated goldens — the repo's first real cross-libm gate (locally the deviation is 0.0 because Rust and CPython share one system libm; on the Linux runner the UCRT goldens make it a genuine cross-libm measurement). All 20 goldens pass their tier on that job. See docs/native-port-reference.md.

_reference_flip._comment: ⚠ The roles in every `evidence` string below were INVERTED by the reference flip, slice 5 (2026-08-16, docs/plans/post-roadmap-reference-flip.md). Those strings were written in Phase 7, when the golden was PYTHON's output and Rust was the candidate being checked against it; the 18 goldens Rust can emit are now Rust's own bytes, so the golden IS the reference and Python is the checker. Read every 'Rust-vs-Python bit-exact locally' below as a statement about the two ports agreeing, which is still true and was re-measured on 2026-08-16 — not as a claim about which side wrote the file. The comparator's argument order says the same thing: `compare.compare(reference=golden, candidate=port)` now has Rust on the reference side.

python_diverges._comment: ⚠ The two goldens Python does NOT reproduce byte-for-byte since they were regenerated from Rust. Their Python-side gates are tolerance comparisons at a 1e-14 last-bit-noise ceiling (1000x tighter than the Tier-2 band here), NOT at the band below. The roster lives in `tests/golden_platform.PYTHON_DIVERGES` and is checked in both directions.

_reference_flip.bands_unchanged: ⚠ The bands themselves are NOT re-derived by the flip, and the plan's stated reason for re-measuring them was factually wrong. `post-roadmap-reference-flip.md` §5 says the bands were 'measured as ±1-ULP sensitivity propagated through the Rust-side transcendentals'; `measure_tier2_bands.py` is pure Python and shims CPython's own `math`, so the basis was always Python-side. What it measures is how far a one-ULP libm disagreement moves a TRAJECTORY — a property of the scenario's dynamics, not of the language — and the two engines are demonstrably running the same arithmetic (16/18 goldens byte-identical, 18/18 within 2 ULP, and slice 1's per-step export walks 2440 steps of the perennial scenario with zero bitwise divergence). So the basis survives the inversion and the numbers were re-measured rather than re-derived; see `measured_2026_08_16`.

measured_2026_08_16.greenhouse: 2.815e-16 against the 2.7e-15 recorded HERE — but docs/native-port-reference.md already carries 2.8e-16, corrected 2026-08-15.
measured_2026_08_16.biosphere_perennial_15yr: 3.520e-15 against the 6.7e-14 recorded HERE — the same doc already carries 3.5e-15.
measured_2026_08_16._the_finding: ⚠⚠ The stale half was THIS FILE, and it is the half that calls itself authoritative. Both figures had been re-measured and corrected in docs/native-port-reference.md (2026-08-14, the light path; 2026-08-15, the layered canopy) and neither correction reached the `evidence` strings here — while this file's own `_comment` and that doc both say tiers.json is the authoritative source and the doc's prose must not contradict it. So the two prose halves of one contract disagreed for two days, in the direction nobody would check. ⚠ The GATES were never stale: test_crossport.py re-derives every sensitivity from the tree and asserts `band > sensitivity` (and, since the layered canopy made one read exactly 0.0, that it is non-zero) — for the Step-3 keys, the biosphere set, the station-energy set and the greenhouse-borrowing set alike. Nothing was unguarded and no band moved; what rotted was the record of why each band is where it is. Third stale-prose finding on this file in two slices, and the first where a CORRECTED copy already existed elsewhere in the repo.
